title: OpenAI's dot assistant burned 300K+ tokens in a day without a single prompt
key_facts: Geordie, an AI agent security and governance company, has tested OpenAI's always-on assistant dot since OpenAI announced it in September.

In its test dot had read-only permissions and no link to personal apps, email or Slack; one dot agent produced 155 activity sequences (traces) and used more than 300,000 tokens in a day with no further human interaction.
The 155 traces cost Geordie about 307,000 tokens; at least 50 of them fell within a two-minute period and most within a couple of hours.

Dot always runs at least two agents, one that talks to the user and one that collects data in the background, and it spun up short-lived sub-agents, for example one that checked all code repositories in a development system.

The Register says roughly 200,000 tokens on a dot based on OpenAI's Astra model cost between $5 and $10; Geordie's chief AI officer Hanah-Marie Darley compared a day of such spending to the price of a latte.
Darley says dot is more proactive than Meta's Muse or Grok Bot, but that this does not necessarily mean higher token use.
Darley's advice: give agents no personal information you would not send in an email, and do not give them real payment cards.
quote_evidence: one dot agent produced 155 separate activity sequences and consumed more than 300,000 tokens - all without further human interaction, and all in the course of a day.
The 155 traces cost Geordie about 307,000 tokens.
“The user would have no idea that there were sub-agents working on their behalf,” she added.
why_it_matters_hint: Always-on assistants start their own background work, so a user or employer can pay for activity they never asked for or saw.
event_date: Geordie's test; reported 13 Oct 2026 (exact test day not stated)
notes: Full text read. One vendor's test of one setup; the figures come from Geordie via interview, not an independent check. No OpenAI comment in the article.
